claim.pdf_says: COMPUTE Format 1 (arithmetic-compute), 14.9.8.2. The SIZE ERROR block is printed as ONE tall square bracket spanning BOTH alternative lines, with a full-height vertical choice-indicator bar immediately inside each bracket:  [ |  ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1 / NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2  | ]  followed on the next line by  [ END-COMPUTE ] .
claim.markdown_says:
```
⌈⌊ ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1        ⌉⌋
⌈⌊ NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2    ⌉⌋
[ END-COMPUTE ]
```
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.4 a pair of vertical bars just inside a bracket means zero or more of the enclosed alternatives may be specified, each at most once, in any order. The transcription drops both bars and additionally repeats the SAME corner glyph pair (⌈⌊ / ⌉⌋) on BOTH rows, so instead of one bracket-with-choice-bars spanning two alternatives the markdown depicts two independent malformed brackets. The choice-indicator semantics are unrecoverable, and a reader following the bracket-without-bars convention would conclude at most ONE of ON SIZE ERROR / NOT ON SIZE ERROR may be written — falsely restrictive; COBOL permits both on one COMPUTE. Every sibling arithmetic statement in this same markdown file (ADD lines 25474-25475, DIVIDE 26635-26636, MULTIPLY 28741-28742, SUBTRACT 32084-32085) transcribes the identical PDF construct correctly as ⎡| ... |⎤ / ⎣| ... |⎦, which proves the convention exists and that COMPUTE is the outlier.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent inspection of both sources; the claim survives every refutation attempt I tried.

(1) PDF, rendered at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v632/spec_p632.png) and re-cropped at 2x magnification over the Format 1 block: I see exactly one tall square bracket whose upper-left corner sits above 'ON SIZE ERROR' and whose lower-left corner sits below 'NOT ON SIZE ERROR' — a SINGLE bracket spanning both stacked alternatives. Immediately inside the left bracket there is one continuous full-height vertical rule spanning both text rows, and mirrored on the right there is a matching full-height vertical rule immediately inside the right bracket. That is unambiguously the ISO choice-indicator notation (bracket + bar pair), not two per-row brackets. '[ END-COMPUTE ]' is printed on its own line below and outside the bracket. The claim's description of the PDF is accurate.

(2) Markdown: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 26209-26213 (= E:/Temp/specrecon/v632/page-632.md lines 21-25) are quoted verbatim and correctly by the claim. I dumped the codepoints: BOTH rows are U+2308 (LEFT CEILING) U+230A (LEFT FLOOR) ... U+2309 (RIGHT CEILING) U+230B (RIGHT FLOOR). There is no U+007C '|' and no vertical-bar character of any kind anywhere in the block. The two rows are glyph-for-glyph identical in their delimiters, so the transcription cannot even be charitably read as a top-corner/bottom-corner split of one tall bracket (which would be ⌈...⌉ on row 1 and ⌊...⌋ on row 2, and would at least depict a well-formed bracket). It is a doubled-corner artifact: each row carries a ceiling AND a floor glyph on each side.

(3) The semantic consequence is real and normative. 5.2.6.4 in this same file (line 2703) reads: 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. ... When enclosed by brackets, zero or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative may be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' Strip the bars and the surviving construct — a bracket around two stacked alternatives — reads as at-most-ONE. So the transcription silently converts 'you may write both ON SIZE ERROR and NOT ON SIZE ERROR on one COMPUTE' into 'you may write at most one of them'. General formats are normative, so severity=normative is correct.

(4) Refutation attempts that FAILED: the bars are not reflowed onto an adjacent line (I read the whole fenced block and the surrounding lines 26204-26219); this is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation — the entire diagram is on one page in both sources; the claim does not misquote either source; and there is NO compensating prose. Unlike ADD, which carries an explicit '> **Figure notes (ISO 5.2.6.4)**' paragraph at line 25482 spelling out that the bars mean both phrases may appear, the COMPUTE block at 26212-26219 goes straight from '[ END-COMPUTE ]' to 'Format 2 (boolean-compute):' with no figure note at all. Nothing in the markdown recovers the dropped semantics.

(5) The claim's 'sibling convention' argument is sound, but its line citations are off by roughly three lines: the cited numbers (25474-25475, 26635-26636, 28741-28742, 32084-32085) point at the identifier-1/literal-1 brace rows of the same format diagrams, not the SIZE ERROR rows. The correct sibling lines are ADD 25477-25478, DIVIDE 25493-25494 / 25507-25508 / 26638-26639, MULTIPLY 28744-28745, SUBTRACT 32087-32088, all of which render '⎡|  ON SIZE ERROR ... |⎤' / '⎣|  NOT ON SIZE ERROR ... |⎦' with explicit ASCII pipes. The substance of the argument is therefore confirmed — the convention exists and COMPUTE departs from it — only the anchors were misnumbered.

This is a genuine content discrepancy, not a formatting nit.
verdict.corrected_description: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 26210-26211 (page 632, 14.9.8.2 COMPUTE Format 1, arithmetic-compute) lose the choice indicators from the ON SIZE ERROR group. The PDF prints ONE tall square bracket spanning both stacked alternatives with a continuous full-height vertical bar immediately inside each bracket edge — the 5.2.6.4 choice-indicator notation meaning zero or more of the enclosed alternatives, each at most once, in any order. The markdown instead emits '⌈⌊ ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1 ⌉⌋' and '⌈⌊ NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2 ⌉⌋' — identical delimiters on both rows (U+2308 U+230A ... U+2309 U+230B), containing no vertical-bar character at all. Because the delimiters are identical on both rows, this is not a top/bottom corner split of one tall bracket but a doubled-corner OCR artifact that depicts two malformed per-row brackets. A reader applying the plain-bracket convention concludes at most ONE of ON SIZE ERROR / NOT ON SIZE ERROR may be written on a COMPUTE, which is falsely restrictive. No figure note compensates: unlike ADD (which carries an explicit 5.2.6.4 figure note at line 25482), the COMPUTE block has none. Fix by adopting the convention already used for the sibling arithmetic statements — ADD 25477-25478, DIVIDE 25493-25494 / 25507-25508 / 26638-26639, MULTIPLY 28744-28745, SUBTRACT 32087-32088 — namely '⎡|  ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1      |⎤' / '⎣|  NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2  |⎦', and add the matching figure note. Two corrections to the claim as filed: (a) its sibling line citations are off by about three lines (25474-25475, 26635-26636, 28741-28742, 32084-32085 are the identifier/literal brace rows, not the SIZE ERROR rows); (b) this COMPUTE block is not the only instance of the defect — DIVIDE Format 4 and Format 5 at lines 26705-26706 and 26719-26720 exhibit the same dropped-bar corruption with a different glyph set ('⌐⌐ ... ¬¬' / '⌊⌊ ... ┘┘'), so the fix should be swept across all of them. Separately and more minorly, the fenced block also drops the PDF's underlining of the required words SIZE, ERROR, NOT and END-COMPUTE, which sibling entries such as SUBTRACT record in a figure note (line 32092).
